author: jsign
content:
Mmm thinking more about costs, I think some assumptions we had before aren't quite correct... mainly with 8037.

Train of thought:
- CPSB=1530, so creating a slot costs 64*1530=97920 gas.
- A validator item needs 5 slots and a builder one 4 (i.e: ~490k and ~392k gas).
- That is only the state creation. Adding the SSTORE/SLOAD costs, calldata, etc, a registration is ~664k gas for validators and ~553k for builders.

So that puts all registrations before the queue is drained at ~0.6M gas, mostly coming from state creation due to 8037...

So.. in reality, we are going to try pushing people to register as soon as the contract is available (e.g. before H* maybe)... so most people will pay that cost, since the queue isn't draining and you're always creating slots.
After H* activates we'll start draining, but until the queue is empty people will continue to pay this. After the queue resets things get better, since you re-write existing slots (~180k gas, or ~370k for the first one of each block).

Note none of this isnt "new" and all other queues behave the same, with a different "amplification factor" of how many slots an item needs... but for this contract we have this reality of a long queue piling up before we start draining.

The same applies to a spammer. A block fits at most gas_limit/490k new validator items (i.e: ~122 at 60M, ~306 at 150M), and we dequeue 1024 per block. So, even someone filling every block before the fork adds 12-30% of what we drain later.

Ofc, not sure we can know cost In USD, since is  somewhat TBD... as in, which gas price will land in reality after gas limti increases.

author: jsign
content:
Long way of saying that maybe we _could_ remove the fixed fee idea and have one less thing to agree on, and difference with existing queues. It also avoids charging more to the people that register early, which is what we want them to do. But I would say is hard to say until we know gas prices implication of gas limit increases in mainnet... so not sure.

(And I guess all depends too on what happens with 8037 in ACD too...)

Sorry for the long brain download. Maybe I'll write all this more clearly in a HackMD doc reg costs in some scenarios (i.e. pre PQ activation when we start draining, and after etc).
